context.objective: Document invoice intake, checks, decisions, exceptions and handoff to Treasury.
context.background: Synthetic example only. All names, roles, systems, amounts and process details are fictional.

turns.text: What process are we documenting, and who is accountable for it?

This is invoice approval and payment handoff, also called AP invoice sign-off. The accounts payable manager is accountable from supplier receipt through Treasury's acceptance of the approved payment package. Treasury's payment execution is a separate process. The purpose is to send accurate, authorized supplier invoices to Treasury without paying the same invoice twice.
What starts the work and what happens when an invoice arrives?

A supplier email to the shared AP mailbox starts a case. Each business day by 10 a.m. the AP analyst saves the invoice in the invoice folder and enters supplier, invoice number, amount and receipt date in the invoice register with status Received. The analyst uses the register to route the case into the duplicate check.
How is a duplicate treated?

The AP analyst searches the invoice register for the same supplier and invoice number. A matching earlier invoice is a duplicate: the analyst links the two entries, sends the supplier a duplicate notice, marks the new entry Duplicate closed, and ends that case. If there is no match, the analyst marks it New and starts the purchase-order and receipt match.
What is checked and how are mismatches resolved?

For a new invoice, the AP analyst compares supplier, amount and line items with the purchase order in the purchasing system and receipt in the receiving register. The analyst records the outcome in the invoice register. A complete match goes to the value decision. For a mismatch the analyst marks Hold and opens a case in the exception log, sends the buyer the difference, and follows up daily. The buyer obtains a corrected invoice or receiving record, records the resolution in the exception log, and returns it to AP. The analyst repeats the match before the hold is released.
Describe the approval routes and any extra checks.

The AP analyst checks the invoice value in the register. Below $50,000 the matched invoice goes directly to the department manager. At $50,000 or above, the controller first checks the matched package in the invoice folder and records an approve or reject decision in the approval register. A controller approval goes to the department manager; a controller rejection goes to the correction route. The approval matrix requires this threshold. This extra controller review adds one business day of staff effort, is included in the existing AP service with no separate charge, and remains mandatory for high-value invoices. Both routes are variations of the same invoice process.
What happens with the manager's decision and a rejected invoice?

The department manager reviews the matched invoice and purchase order from the invoice folder through the approval portal and records Approve or Reject. For either controller or manager rejection, the AP analyst records the reason in the exception log, sends it to the buyer, and sets status Correction required. The buyer resolves the reason with the supplier or receiving department and returns corrected documents to AP. The analyst then repeats the purchase-order and receipt match; the invoice follows the value and approval decisions again.
How does the process finish after approval?

After manager approval, the AP analyst saves the manager decision and any controller decision with the invoice and purchase order in the invoice folder, marks the register Ready for Treasury, and sends the package link through the Treasury queue. A Treasury analyst checks that the package link opens and records Accepted in the queue. AP marks the case Handed off and closes it when that acceptance is recorded. The package and register remain available as the handoff evidence.
What controls and supporting proof are retained?

The duplicate search, three-way match, value threshold and manager approval are required controls. The controller review is required at the high-value threshold. The AP analyst prepares the package, while the department manager approves it; the controller separately reviews high-value items. The register, exception log, approval register, portal decisions and Treasury acceptance provide the evidence for each check and handoff.
How are delays and escalation handled?

The AP analyst checks open holds and rejections each business day. If a buyer has not supplied corrected material by the end of the second business day, the analyst escalates the exception log entry to the AP manager. The manager assigns a backup buyer and records the assignment in the log; the backup returns the correction to AP for the same recheck. Standard matched invoices target handoff within two business days, and high-value invoices target three business days.
What are the main pain points and their effects?

The analyst copies invoice details from email into the register and follows up on exceptions manually. These activities consume about fifteen minutes of staff effort per invoice and are the main reported friction. Waiting for corrected documents is the main source of delay; the team tracks overdue cases in the exception log.
What is the impact if the work fails or is delayed?

A duplicate payment can cause cash loss and recovery work. An incorrect or unapproved invoice can cause a supplier dispute or inaccurate payment. A late handoff can delay supplier payment. The AP manager reviews these risks with the team each month using the exception log.
What existing materials guide or document this work?

The AP operating procedure describes the steps and escalation. The invoice register template, exception log template, approval matrix, purchase order, receiving register, portal decision record and Treasury queue receipt document the work. The AP manager maintains the procedure and templates.
Is there anything else needed to understand this process?

That covers the process from supplier email to Treasury acceptance, including duplicate closure, mismatch rework, the high-value approval route, manager rejection, escalation and the evidence retained. Treasury executes payment as a separate process.

summary: AP receives and logs supplier invoices, closes duplicates, resolves mismatches through buyer rework, applies controller review at the high-value threshold, obtains manager approval, and closes after Treasury accepts the documented handoff.

steps.title: Receive and register invoice
steps.system: Shared AP mailbox, invoice folder and invoice register
steps.description: Save the supplier invoice and record its identifying details by 10 a.m. each business day.
steps.input: Supplier invoice email and attachment
steps.output: Invoice filed and register entry marked Received
steps.completion_criteria: Supplier, invoice number, amount and receipt date are recorded and the file is saved
steps.handoff: AP analyst moves the registered invoice to the duplicate check

steps.title: Is this a duplicate invoice?
steps.description: Search for an earlier entry with the same supplier and invoice number.
steps.input: Received invoice and supplier/invoice number
steps.output: Duplicate or new classification
steps.completion_criteria: Register search establishes whether a matching earlier entry exists
steps.handoff: Duplicate goes to closure; new invoice goes to the three-way match

steps.title: Close duplicate case
steps.description: Link the new and earlier entries, notify the supplier and close the new case.
steps.input: Duplicate classification and earlier register entry
steps.output: Linked entry, supplier notice and Duplicate closed status
steps.completion_criteria: Entries are linked, notice sent and new case marked Duplicate closed
steps.handoff: Case ends; supplier receives the duplicate notice

steps.title: Do invoice, order and receipt match?
steps.system: Purchasing system, receiving register and invoice register
steps.description: Compare supplier, amount and line items on the invoice, purchase order and receiving record.
steps.input: New or corrected invoice, purchase order and receiving record
steps.output: Match or mismatch decision
steps.completion_criteria: All three records are compared and the outcome recorded for routing
steps.handoff: Match goes to value decision; mismatch goes to buyer correction

steps.title: Resolve mismatch and release hold
steps.actor: AP analyst and buyer; AP manager for escalation
steps.description: Record the difference, follow up daily and receive corrected material; escalate after two business days and use the assigned backup buyer when required.
steps.input: Mismatch details, invoice, purchase order and receiving record
steps.output: Corrected invoice or receiving record and documented exception resolution
steps.completion_criteria: Buyer returns corrected material and the resolution is recorded in the exception log
steps.handoff: Buyer returns corrected material to AP, which repeats the match before releasing the hold

steps.title: Does the value require controller review?
steps.description: Route matched invoices by the $50,000 value threshold.
steps.input: Matched invoice and recorded amount
steps.output: Standard or high-value route
steps.completion_criteria: Amount is compared with the threshold
steps.handoff: Below $50,000 goes to manager; $50,000 or above goes to controller

steps.title: Review high-value invoice
steps.description: Review the matched high-value package and record an approval or rejection.
steps.input: Matched invoice package of $50,000 or more
steps.output: Controller approval or rejection recorded
steps.completion_criteria: Controller records the decision in the approval register
steps.handoff: Approval goes to the manager; rejection goes to AP correction

steps.title: Approve or reject invoice
steps.description: Review the matched invoice and purchase order and record the decision.
steps.input: Matched invoice and purchase order, with controller approval for high-value items
steps.output: Manager approval or rejection in the portal
steps.completion_criteria: Manager records Approve or Reject
steps.handoff: Approval goes to AP for package handoff; rejection goes to correction

steps.title: Correct a rejected invoice
steps.system: Exception log and supplier or receiving communications
steps.description: Record the rejection, send the reason to the buyer and obtain corrected documents for another match.
steps.input: Controller or manager rejection and its reason
steps.output: Correction required status, documented reason and corrected documents
steps.completion_criteria: Reason is logged and corrected documents are returned to AP
steps.handoff: Buyer returns the correction to AP for matching and a fresh approval route

steps.title: Save approvals and send package
steps.system: Invoice folder, invoice register and Treasury queue
steps.description: File approval evidence, mark the invoice ready and send the package link to Treasury.
steps.input: Manager approval, controller approval when required, invoice and purchase order
steps.output: Filed package, Ready for Treasury status and queue handoff
steps.completion_criteria: Required decisions are filed and the package link is sent in the Treasury queue
steps.handoff: Treasury analyst receives the package link for acceptance

steps.title: Accept handoff and close case
steps.description: Treasury opens the package link and records acceptance; AP closes its case.
steps.input: Treasury queue package link and register entry
steps.output: Treasury Accepted receipt and AP Handed off status
steps.completion_criteria: Treasury records Accepted and AP marks the case Handed off
steps.handoff: AP case closes; Treasury proceeds with its separate payment process

exceptions: Duplicates are linked, notified and closed without entering the payment route.
Mismatches and rejected invoices return to the buyer for correction and to AP for a repeated match.
Open corrections are followed up daily and escalated to the AP manager after two business days.
controls: Search the register for a duplicate supplier and invoice number.
Match the invoice to the purchase order and receiving record before approval.
Controller reviews invoices at or above $50,000; department manager approves every payment package.
Retain approval and Treasury-acceptance evidence; AP preparation and manager approval are separate roles.
